expectations.text: Output does NOT recommend Full rollout — the combination of sub-MDE effect (+0.6pp vs planned +2.0pp MDE) and high implementation cost must prevent a full rollout recommendation
expectations.evidence: Recommendation explicitly states 'REJECT (Do Not Proceed)' and 'Do not proceed with rollout. The current feature does not justify its implementation cost.'

expectations.text: Output explicitly addresses the gap between the observed effect (+0.6pp) and the pre-specified MDE (+2.0pp), and explains that the MDE represents the business-value threshold for this feature
expectations.evidence: Section 'The Effect Size vs. MDE Gap' states: 'The observed effect of +0.6 percentage points represents only 30% of the pre-specified MDE threshold of +2.0pp. This MDE was established as the business-value threshold—the minimum lift required to justify the feature's value... The MDE represents the point at which the business believes the feature becomes worth building; falling short of it means we have not cleared that bar.'

expectations.text: Output does not treat statistical significance (p=0.038) as sufficient justification for proceeding — the economic case for shipping must also hold
expectations.evidence: Section 'Statistical Significance ≠ Business Significance' explicitly states: 'The p-value of 0.038 tells us the result is unlikely due to chance, but statistical significance does not equate to business significance... it does not validate that the detected effect is meaningful relative to implementation costs.'

expectations.text: Output considers the implementation cost (HIGH, 6–8 engineering weeks) relative to the sub-threshold effect size and concludes the ROI case is weak
expectations.evidence: Section 'Implementation Cost Analysis' states: 'The estimated 6–8 weeks of engineering effort represents a substantial investment... The ROI case for shipping a feature that underperforms its pre-specified economic threshold is weak, particularly when that investment could be directed toward higher-impact opportunities.'

expectations.text: Output recommends Reject or Iterate (not rollout), and explains that the current result does not justify the implementation investment
expectations.evidence: Recommendation section states 'REJECT' and explains: 'Do not proceed with rollout. The current feature does not justify its implementation cost.' Next Steps section offers Iterate/Redesign as an alternative path.
